stories.headline: Meta launches Muse Image and previews Muse Video, its first Superintelligence Labs media models

key_facts.fact: On July 7, 2026 Meta launched Muse Image and previewed Muse Video, the first media generation models built by Meta Superintelligence Labs, the division led by Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang.
key_facts.excerpt: We're excited to launch Muse Image and preview Muse Video, the first media generation models developed by Meta Superintelligence Labs.

key_facts.fact: Muse Image works as an agent rather than a direct prompt-to-pixel model: it calls search and coding tools, self-refines its own drafts, and improves with more test-time compute. Meta says the self-refinement behavior was not designed but emerged during reinforcement learning.
key_facts.excerpt: Instead of directly mapping prompts to images, Muse Image operates as an agent: it invokes search and coding tools to improve accuracy, self-refines its own generations, and improves through scaling test-time compute. ... We didn't design this behavior. Instead, it emerged during RL training simply because self-refinement produced better images and therefore higher reward.

key_facts.fact: Meta says Muse Image holds the No. 2 spot on Arena for text-to-image, single-image editing and multi-image editing on human-preference Elo (rankings as of July 5, 2026), while Muse Video ranks No. 3 for text-to-video.
key_facts.excerpt: Muse Image holds the No. 2 spot on Arena for text-to-image, single-image editing, and multi-image editing as measured by human preference Elo rankings at the time of writing. ... On Arena, Muse Video ranks No. 3 in human-preference Elo for text-to-video at the time of writing.

key_facts.fact: Muse Image is live in the Meta AI app and meta.ai, in Instagram Stories in the US, and on WhatsApp in a limited number of countries, with Facebook coming soon. Muse Video is 'coming soon' to creators and Meta AI.
key_facts.excerpt: Muse Image is available today across the Meta AI app and on meta.ai, Instagram Stories in the US, and WhatsApp in limited countries, and is coming soon to Facebook. Muse Video is coming soon to creators and Meta AI.

key_facts.fact: Every Muse Image output carries Content Seal, an invisible watermark Meta says survives cropping, compression, resizing and screenshotting; Meta previewed a web detection tool to check for it. Content Seal is not compatible with SynthID or C2PA Content Credentials, the watermarking standards used by rivals.
key_facts.excerpt: This watermarking system, called Content Seal, remains in place "even when cropped, compressed, resized, or screenshotted" ... Content Seal is not compatible with SynthID or C2PA Content Credentials, two established watermarking methods used by other companies.

key_facts.fact: The model lets users generate images featuring friends or creators from their publicly available Instagram posts; people who do not want their content remixed must opt out in settings. Advertisers get access via Advantage+ in the coming weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: The most notable feature lets users create images featuring friends or creators based on their publicly available Instagram posts. Those who do not want their content reused or remixed by AI can opt out in the settings menu.

key_facts.fact: Muse Image is the second model shipped by Meta Superintelligence Labs, after the Muse Spark large language model that debuted in April; Wang was hired to lead the lab a year ago after Meta invested billions and recruited researchers on packages exceeding $200 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta's Superintelligence Labs debuted its first large language model, Muse Spark, in April ... after Meta invested billions and hired several researchers with compensation packages exceeding $200 million.

stories.headline: US Commerce clears OpenAI's GPT-5.6 for broad release; Sol, Terra and Luna launch Thursday

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced late on Tuesday, July 7, that its GPT-5.6 flagship model Sol, plus the lower tiers Terra and Luna, will launch publicly on Thursday.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI announced late Tuesday night that GPT-5.6 flagship model Sol, as well as lower tiers Terra and Luna, will launch publicly this Thursday.

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration gave OpenAI the green light for a broad launch after additional testing by the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) inside the Commerce Department; OpenAI sent technical experts who stayed in Washington to answer questions.
key_facts.excerpt: Testing was done by the Center for AI Standards and Innovation within the Department of Commerce, with OpenAI sending technical experts who have remained in D.C. to address potential questions, the source said.

key_facts.fact: Until now GPT-5.6 was available only to about 20 partners whose names were individually approved by the US government — the first time an American lab gated a frontier model behind a state-approved roster.
key_facts.excerpt: Until now the model had been available only through about 20 partners whose names were individually approved by the US government. ... the first time an American lab had gated a frontier model behind a state-approved roster.

key_facts.fact: The review sits inside a framework the Trump administration established on June 2, which introduced a voluntary pre-release check of up to 30 days for 'covered frontier models'. This is its first live test.
key_facts.excerpt: It is the first big test of President Trump's June executive order, which lets developers submit 'covered frontier models' for up to 30 days of federal review.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.6 is a three-tier family: Sol is the flagship, Terra a lower-cost mid-tier for everyday enterprise workloads, and Luna the fastest and cheapest, aimed at high-volume tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-5.6 is a three-tier family rather than a single model. Sol is the flagship, Terra a lower-cost mid-tier option, and Luna the fastest and cheapest of the three.

key_facts.fact: The Commerce Department in June banned foreigners from accessing Anthropic's Mythos and Fable models, forcing their withdrawal from the market; the Fable ban was lifted last week and customer access restored a day later.
key_facts.excerpt: The Commerce Department in June banned foreigners from having access to Anthropic's Mythos and Fable models, essentially forcing their withdrawal from the market. The ban on Fable was lifted last week, with customer access restored one day later.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI had said the staggered rollout imposed last month was not its preferred way to release models, arguing that firms and government are operating before concrete release standards called for in Trump's AI executive order have been finalized.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said at the time that the staggered rollout was not its preferred way to release new models. The company also said AI firms and the government are operating before more concrete standards for releasing such models — called for in President Trump's latest AI executive order — have been finalized.

stories.headline: SpaceXAI and Cursor to ship their first jointly built frontier model, per internal memo

key_facts.fact: SpaceXAI and Cursor plan to launch their first jointly developed AI model as soon as Wednesday, July 8, according to a memo sent to staff reported by The Information on July 7.
key_facts.excerpt: Exclusive: SpaceXAI Plans to Launch New Model with Cursor as Soon as Wednesday

key_facts.fact: The companies had pushed back the launch earlier in the week in order to improve the model's efficiency; the model is expected to process information quickly, making it competitive with Anthropic's Opus 4.8 and OpenAI's GPT-5.5.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies had pushed back plans to launch the model earlier this week in order to improve its efficiency, added the report published on Tuesday. ... the new model is expected to process information quickly, making it competitive in some respects with Anthropic's Opus 4.8 and OpenAI's GPT 5.5, according to the report.

key_facts.fact: It would be the first model built jointly with Cursor, the AI coding startup SpaceX is acquiring for $60 billion in an all-stock deal announced in June. A Grok model shipped in May had already incorporated Cursor data, per Elon Musk.
key_facts.excerpt: This one, according to the Information, is the first SpaceXAI model built jointly with the AI startup Cursor, which SpaceX is currently in the process of acquiring for $60 billion. A version of the Grok AI model that shipped in May did at least incorporate data from Cursor, according to Elon Musk.

key_facts.fact: SpaceXAI is the rebranding of the company formerly known as xAI, announced on Monday, July 6.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceXAI is a rebranding of the company formerly known as xAI. It was announced Monday.

key_facts.fact: Cursor founder Michael Truell said last month the company was building a model to compete with frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI, calling it the 'next phase of the company' without linking it publicly to SpaceXAI.
key_facts.excerpt: Cursor founder Michael Truell made an announcement last month of a model Cursor was working on that would supposedly compete with Frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI. He referred to this as the 'next phase of the company'.

key_facts.fact: Reuters could not independently verify the report; Cursor declined to comment and SpaceXAI did not immediately respond.
key_facts.excerpt: Cursor declined to comment when contacted by Reuters, while SpaceXAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

key_facts.fact: As of 10:28 UTC on July 8 the model had not yet been released, with news accounts still describing it as 'set to launch' per The Information.
key_facts.excerpt: JUST IN: Elon Musk's SpaceXAI and Cursor are set to launch their first jointly built AI model as soon as Wednesday, per The Information.

stories.headline: Microsoft starts swapping OpenAI and Anthropic models for its own MAI models in Excel and Outlook

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on July 7 that Microsoft is moving away from OpenAI's and Anthropic's most advanced models in favor of its in-house MAI family, citing a person familiar with the company's AI strategy who said Microsoft has grown increasingly concerned about the cost of top-tier third-party models.
key_facts.excerpt: That's according to a report today by Bloomberg, which cited a person familiar with the company's AI strategy as saying that it has become increasingly concerned about the cost of using top-tier models from OpenAI and Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: 'Tens of thousands of prompts' in platforms such as Excel and Outlook that were previously routed through third-party models are now handled by Microsoft's MAI models to save costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Apparently, "tens of thousands of prompts" in platforms such as Excel and Outlook, which were previously routed through third-party models, are now being handled by Microsoft's MAI models in an effort to save costs, the person said.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman told Bloomberg last month: 'Anthropic is extremely expensive and I think many people are urgently looking for alternatives. We pay a lot of money to Anthropic, so our goal is to reduce and ultimately eliminate that cost.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Anthropic is extremely expensive and I think many people are urgently looking for alternatives," Microsoft AI Chief Executive Mustafa Suleyman told Bloomberg in an interview last month. "We pay a lot of money to Anthropic, so our goal is to reduce and ultimately eliminate that cost."

key_facts.fact: The in-house models still handle only a small fraction of total requests. MAI models are also live in GitHub Copilot, and a proprietary transcription model is expected to ship in Teams soon.
key_facts.excerpt: The in-house models still handle only a small fraction of total requests, but Microsoft wants to keep cutting its spending on third-party AI over time. The MAI models are also available in GitHub Copilot, and a proprietary transcription model is expected to ship in Teams soon.

key_facts.fact: SiliconANGLE notes MAI-Thinking-1 is a midsized model with 35 billion active parameters that Microsoft says matched the coding capabilities of Anthropic's Claude Opus in blind tests, even as Microsoft publicly asserts its models aren't as sophisticated as leading frontier systems.
key_facts.excerpt: describes MAI-Thinking ... 1 as a midsized ... 35 billion active parameters ... In blind tests, it matched the coding capabilities of Anthropic's Claude Opus ... despite publicly asserting that those models aren't as sophisticated as other leading frontier AI systems.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI charges $5 per million input tokens and $30 per million output tokens for GPT-5.5, and Microsoft gets a partnership discount, but the costs still add up; Microsoft's deal with OpenAI expires in 2032.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI charges a lot less than Anthropic, with GPT-5.5 costing $5 per million input tokens and $30 per million output tokens. ... Moreover, Microsoft's deal with OpenAI will ultimately expire in 2032.

key_facts.fact: For Copilot and Office customers this could mean paying the same amount for weaker AI; CEO Satya Nadella has hinted AI billing could shift toward usage-based pricing, with cheaper MAI models as the default and third-party models as paid add-ons.
key_facts.excerpt: For Copilot and Office customers, this could mean paying the same amount for weaker AI so that Microsoft can lower its own costs. ... Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella also hinted that AI billing could shift further toward usage-based pricing instead of flat-rate subscriptions. One possible setup would make cheaper MAI models the default, with third-party models from OpenAI or Anthropic available as premium add-ons at extra cost.

stories.headline: Anthropic brings Claude Cowork to web and mobile, says 90%+ of its use isn't software development

key_facts.fact: On July 7 Anthropic began rolling out Claude Cowork to web and mobile in beta, with sessions running remotely so files and work follow the user across devices. Access starts with Max plan subscribers over the next several weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Cowork is rolling out to mobile and web so your sessions and files go where you go, on any device. Beta access is rolling out over the next several weeks starting with Max users, with more plans to follow.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says more than 90% of Cowork usage is not software development. The largest categories are business operations and content creation, which together account for roughly half of all usage.
key_facts.excerpt: AI agents made their name writing code. But when we looked at how people use Claude Cowork, more than 90% of it wasn't software development. Most of it was everyday knowledge work, and the largest categories were business operations and content creation ... Together, that's roughly half of all usage.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic surveyed 1.2 million anonymized Cowork sessions in May. Software development accounted for 8.7% of usage, DevOps and cloud infrastructure 7%, research and intelligence 6.4%, document processing and extraction 4.1%, and sales/revenue operations 4%.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic released Cowork in January 2026 and in May, the company surveyed 1.2 million anonymized sessions ... The remaining top categories included software development at 8.7%, DevOps and cloud infrastructure ... at 7%, research and intelligence at 6.4%, document processing and extraction at 4.1%, and sales revenue operations at 4%.

key_facts.fact: Cowork keeps working in the background even when the laptop is closed or the phone is off, letting a user start a task at a desk and steer it from a phone.
key_facts.excerpt: users can kick off a task at their desk, check on it from their phone, and pull up the finished result in a browser anywhere. Claude keeps working in the background even when the laptop is closed or the phone is turned off.

key_facts.fact: The desktop app remains required for local capabilities — reading and writing files in connected folders, local connectors and plugins, browser control through Claude in Chrome, and Computer Use.
key_facts.excerpt: The desktop app remains essential for features that tap into the local machine ... That includes reading and writing files in connected folders, local connectors and plugins, browser control through Claude in Chrome, and Computer Use.

key_facts.fact: To mark the launch Anthropic is extending doubled Cowork usage limits through August 5.
key_facts.excerpt: To mark the launch, we're extending doubled Cowork usage limits through August 5, so there's plenty of room to try bigger tasks.

key_facts.excerpt: Chinese AI developer MiniMax is working on a new large language model with 2.7 trillion parameters, larger than any other Chinese AI models ...

key_facts.fact: The model is expected to launch in the third quarter of this year and is set to surpass all existing domestic Chinese AI models.
key_facts.excerpt: This model is set to surpass all existing domestic AI models and is expected to be launched in the third quarter of this year. MiniMax plans to ...

key_facts.fact: Reuters picked up the report the same day, noting MiniMax's plan to launch the 2.7-trillion-parameter model.

key_facts.fact: MiniMax's current flagship, M3, was released on May 31, 2026 with roughly 428 billion parameters and about 23 billion activated, a 1-million-token context window and native multimodality — a fraction of the size of the planned model.
key_facts.excerpt: MiniMax-M3 is a native multimodal model with 1M context. It has ~428B parameters and ~23B activated parameters.

key_facts.fact: M3 uses MiniMax Sparse Attention, delivering 9x prefill and 15x decode speedups over M2 at 1M-token context and cutting per-token compute to 1/20.

key_facts.fact: MiniMax positions M3 as reaching frontier-level performance on specialized tasks such as coding and agentic work.

stories.headline: China's industry ministry warns of a 'serious' backdoor risk in Anthropic's Claude Code

key_facts.fact: On Wednesday, July 8, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's Network Security Threat and Vulnerability Information Sharing Platform (NVDB) said it had detected a potential 'backdoor' risk in Claude Code and described the threat as serious.
key_facts.excerpt: The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's Network Security Threat and Vulnerability Information Sharing Platform said on Wednesday that it had detected a potential "backdoor" risk in Claude Code, describing the threat as serious.

key_facts.fact: The regulator said affected versions run from 2.1.91 to 2.1.196 and alleged the tool's built-in monitoring mechanisms could transmit sensitive information — including users' location data and identity-related identifiers — to remote servers without user authorization.
key_facts.excerpt: The NVDB said affected versions range from 2.1.91 to 2.1.196. It alleged that the tool's built-in monitoring mechanisms could transmit sensitive information — including users' location data and identity-related identifiers — to remote servers without user authorization.

key_facts.fact: The platform urged companies and developers to immediately audit their machines, uninstall or upgrade affected versions, and tighten controls over external connections from development tools on critical business networks.
key_facts.excerpt: The platform urged companies and developers using affected versions to immediately conduct security checks and remove the vulnerable versions or upgrade to the latest releases that have eliminated the relevant code. It also advised organizations to tighten controls over external connections from development tools on critical business networks.

key_facts.fact: The warning follows a July 6 report that Anthropic quickly removed a tracker that had secretly monitored Claude Code users in China after a security researcher exposed the hidden code.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic quickly removed a tracker secretly monitoring Claude Code users in China after a security researcher exposed the hidden code.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba had already banned staff from using Claude Code on July 3, listing it as 'high-risk' software after researchers found Anthropic had embedded steganographic tracking code to identify Chinese users.
key_facts.excerpt: The Chinese tech giant has listed Claude Code as 'high-risk' software, after discovering Anthropic had tracked Chinese users using hidden code.

key_facts.fact: Chinese state media framed the alert as an official warning over backdoor security risks in the US startup's AI coding tool.
key_facts.excerpt: China issues warning over backdoor security risks in Anthropic's AI coding tool Claude Code
